newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia looking to repair ties with PNG.
newsitem.headline: Australia looking to repair ties with PNG.

text.p: Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said on Thursday he would seek talks with neighbouring Papua New Guinea's new government as soon as he could to help repair ties battered by a row over mercenaries.

"Our aim is to have a constructive and amicable relationship with PNG and put behind us the tense exchanges of February to April," Downer told a business lunch in this Queensland town on the eve of a South Pacific ministerial forum.
Downer said he hoped to visit Papua New Guinea in mid-August and would discuss economic reforms, Australian aid and the nine-year secessionist war on PNG's Bougainville Island.
Relations between Canberra and Port Moresby soured early this year over Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan's plan to use mercenaries to end the Bougainville rebellion.
The mercenary plan also sparked an army mutiny and civil unrest in PNG, forcing Chan to briefly stand aside during an inquiry into the affair.
Two-week national elections were held in June and a new government is expected to be formed soon after the official election results are announced on July 15.
Partly as a result of the mercenary row, Chan lost his seat in the elections. But he remains prime minister until the results are formally announced.
Australia was Papua New Guinea's colonial master until the South Pacific nation won independence in 1975. It is is also its largest aid donor.
